steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: When Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933, over 6 million Germans were unemployed - nearly 30% of the workforce. By 1939, official unemployment was under 500,000. The Nazis claimed to have solved the unemployment crisis, but the reality was more complex.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazis launched massive public works programmes, most famously the autobahn (motorway) network. Between 1933 and 1938, over 3,000 km of autobahn were built. However, the autobahn programme was originally proposed by the Weimar government - the Nazis simply took credit for it.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Rearmament was the single biggest factor in reducing unemployment. Government spending on arms rose from 3.5 billion marks in 1933 to 30 billion marks by 1939. By 1939, 40% of government expenditure was on the military.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The National Labour Service (RAD) was made compulsory for all men aged 18-25 in June 1935. They had to serve 6 months doing manual labour - building roads, draining marshes, planting forests, and working on farms. They wore military-style uniforms and lived in camps.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two ways the Nazis reduced unemployment. (4 marks) | How important was rearmament in reducing German unemployment? (8 marks) | "Nazi economic policies benefited German workers." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always question the unemployment statistics - they were manipulated by excluding women, Jews, and political opponents Rearmament was MORE important than public works (like autobahns) in reducing unemployment The KdF car (Volkswagen) is a great example of Nazi broken promises - workers saved but never received cars For "did workers benefit" questions, always balance benefits (jobs, leisure) against losses (rights, unions, wages) Remember: the DAF was NOT a trade union - it was a state organisation that represented the regime, not the workers Working hours INCREASED under the Nazis (43 to 49 per week) - workers traded freedom for employment The Four Year Plan (1936) under Göring aimed at autarky (self-sufficiency) - this is important for showing the economy was being prepared for war
